To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
there were no significant effects of principal instructional management on the growth of students in lower socioeconomic status.
only one characteristic, Protecting Instructional Time, of a principal had an effect, a negative effect, on the growth of academic achievement for lower SES students.
the frequency of a principal protecting instructional time had a significant effect on the growth in academic achievement of the lower socioeconomic students.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how principals can impact the growth of lower socioeconomic status students in the area of academics.
the effect of the principal on the academic growth of lower SES student.
how principals impact student achievement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the principal instructional characteristics measured by the PIMRS have no effect on the growth in academic performance of lower SES students in grades three to eight.
the principal instructional management characteristic that protected instructional time did not have a significant effect on the academic growth of lower SES student achievement.
the principal has a small effect on student achievement and that effect is not consistent across all principals and across all student groups.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the characteristics of the principal did not have a significant impact on the growth of academic scores for lower SES students.
principals who protect instructional time may have an impact on the growth of academic scores for lower socioeconomic students.
the characteristics of the principal do not have a direct effect on the growth in the academic achievement of the lower SES student.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the principal does have a significant impact on the academic growth of lower SES student, and the effect is a negative one.
there are many variables that influence student achievement and that the principal is only one of those variables.
there is a need for further investigation into the effect of principal behaviors on student achievement.
